Delightful weather continues as we enjoy a batch of dry, cooler air. Sunday was only the fourth day of the month with a below average high temperature for the date in Boone, and we were just below average today. Temperatures tick warmer for Tuesday & Wednesday, and widely scattered PM showers revive on Wednesday. The humidity does increase some by midweek, but both days should still be quite nice. Another front bears down late in the week, delivering a wetter Thursday.

Forecast Discussion

We have the driest, coolest air since temperatures briefly dipped into the upper 40s and low 50s back at the end of July remains in charge of our weather Monday. It was another very pleasant, mostly sunny afternoon.

Tuesday is a smidge warmer and more humid, but really still very nice compared to the consistently hot & muggy August we have been enduring. An approaching shortwave embedded in our large scale trough over the Eastern U.S. hauls a front southeastward as we push into the second half of the week, and northwest upper flow shuts off beginning late Wednesday ahead of this wave. Widely scattered showers return as southwest flow aloft takes hold.

Thursday is the wettest of the set, with occasional (mostly afternoon) showers & storms popping up in a moist airmass squeezed between the approaching front to our northwest and a drifting warm front to our southeast. Showers wind down into the overnight hours.

The front moves through sometime Friday, but we should still see a few PM showers & storms, as this front does not have the drying power of our most recent one.

A brief period of easterly flow with a handful of isolated showers may try to set up over the weekend as we transition into a warmer pattern thanks to an upper-level ridge moving towards the region.
